Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically lowered serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations were not associated with risk of major depression.
Sentence: "The odds ratio per genetically predicted one standard deviation decrease in S-25OHD concentrations was 1.02 (95% confidence interval 0.97⁻1.08; p = 0.44)."
Measured as: major depression
Population: Individuals of European ancestry from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (59,851 major depression cases and 113,154 controls)
Intervention: Genetically predicted serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations (six SNPs from SUNLIGHT)
Comparator: Per one standard deviation difference in genetically predicted S-25OHD
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 172,005
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Genetically proxied higher 25(OH) vitamin D was associated with lower odds of recurrent major depression, weak evidence using cIVW.
Sentence: "Point estimates for rMDD were the largest magnitude, with three micronutrients suggestive of a protective effect: serum iron (ORcIVW 0.90 per SD increase; 95% CI 0.85-0.95; p = 0.0003); erythrocyte copper (ORcIVW 0.97; 95% CI 0.95-0.99; p = 0.0004); and 25(OH) vitamin D (ORcIVW 0.81; 0.66-0.99; p = 0.04)."
Measured as: recurrent depression (rMDD)
Population: Cases and controls from Psychiatric Genomics Consortium GWAS of recurrent MDD (17,451 cases, 62,482 controls)
Intervention: Genetically proxied 25(OH) vitamin D level per SD increase
Comparator: Lower genetically proxied vitamin D level
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 490,688
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Both studies are Mendelian randomization analyses in Psychiatric Genomics Consortium cohorts, but Study A examines overall major depression whereas Study B restricts its outcome definition to recurrent major depression.",
